dul.name: Dubai Unified Licence
dul.description: A unified digital identity issued to businesses in Dubai, including mainland and free zone companies. The official 12 November 2025 update reported that average business bank-account opening time had fallen from 65 days to 5 days and named seven banks already integrated with DUL.
dul.coverage: All businesses in Dubai, including mainland and free zone companies
dul.average_note: The 5-day figure is a reported programme-wide average, not a service-level guarantee for an individual bank or applicant.
dul.bank_list_note: A bank absent from the 12 November 2025 announcement is not proven to be non-integrated; confirm current integration with DET or the bank.

open_finance.status: Controlled live usage ahead of wider customer availability. First-phase mandate covers all banks (including foreign branches) and insurers.

live_banks.note: First UAE bank fully live in operational use (late 2025), with licensed TPPs Pay10 and Lean Technologies.

live_banks.name: FAB

live_banks.name: ADIB
live_banks.note: First Islamic bank live under Al Tareq (first phase: CBUAE-certified API frameworks for data sharing and transactions).

central_bank_law.scope: New Central Bank law replacing the 2018 law. Expands the CBUAE perimeter to open finance, stablecoin issuance, payment services using virtual assets, DeFi and enabling technology providers. In-scope entities must be licensed, partner with a licensed entity, or exit by the one-year transition deadline of 2026-09-16.

recent_entrants_2026.note: New CBUAE authorisations and product launches in H1 2026. These are NOT full entries in the bank comparison matrix; they are listed for awareness. Most are not yet fully launched for business banking.

entrants.name: Alaan
entrants.licence: Not a bank; account issued by Ruya Community Islamic Bank via ruya BaaS rails
entrants.note: AI business account launched 2026-06-16 (Shariah-compliant, ruya's first major BaaS deal). SuperPay supplier payments to 40+ countries with no transfer fees, AI invoice processing, and integrations with Odoo, Zoho, Xero and QuickBooks.

regulators.note: The UAE Capital Market Authority (CMA) replaces the Securities and Commodities Authority (SCA) effective 2026-01-01 under Federal Decree-Law No. 32 of 2025 (CMA Law) and Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2025 (Capital Market Law). The CMA succeeds to all SCA rights, obligations and contracts; regulated entities have until 2027-01-01 to regularise (extendable by the CMA Board). Banking supervision remains with the CBUAE; DIFC/ADGM-only activities remain out of CMA scope.

banks.name: Wio Business
banks.notes: Best for solo founders with clean profiles. App-only, no physical branches. Islamic banking platform in development (announced March 2026, subject to regulatory approval). June 2026 Geidea partnership distributes Wio Business accounts and SME financing to Geidea merchants. FY2025 revenue AED 1.24 billion; 120,000+ businesses report Wio as their main business banking partner.
